title: Milvus: Open-Source Vector Search at Enterprise Scale

questions.q: Milvus's disaggregated architecture has four layers. Which pairing of layer and responsibility is correct?
options: Worker layer — request routing and load balancing
Coordinator layer — metadata management, segment assignment, and topology
Storage layer — index building on sealed segments
Access layer — durability, WAL, and metadata
questions.explain: The four layers are Access (Proxy: routing/load balancing), Coordinator (Root/Query/Data/Index: metadata, segment assignment, topology), Worker (Query/Data/Index nodes: search, ingest, index build), and Storage (object storage + etcd + message bus: durability, WAL, metadata).

questions.q: Milvus offers eventual consistency by default. What must you do for an application that inserts a record and immediately queries for it?
options: Enable snapshot isolation in the schema
Use the proxy's synchronous mode flag
Set write_consistency_factor to 0
Call collection.flush() to force segment sealing
questions.explain: Because ingestion is streaming via the message bus, newly inserted records are not immediately visible; you must call collection.flush() to force segment sealing when you need insert-then-query visibility.

questions.q: Which index would you pick for a Milvus deployment holding more than 500M vectors that cannot fit in RAM?
options: IVF_SQ8
DISKANN
HNSW
FLAT
questions.explain: The chapter's index table assigns DISKANN to the >500M-vector, cannot-fit-in-RAM case: it serves from SSD with lower cost and ~97% recall, while HNSW is the default for under ~500M vectors.

questions.q: Milvus offers three multi-tenancy patterns. Which statement about them is correct?
options: Partition-per-tenant provides database-level guarantees that queries cannot omit the tenant filter
Field-based filtering is the only pattern; the other two are deprecated
Partitions scale to around 1,024 per collection in Milvus 2.4, fitting SaaS apps with up to several hundred tenants
Collection-per-tenant supports unlimited tenants
questions.explain: Partitions scale to ~1,024 per collection (Milvus 2.4), suiting hundreds of tenants with selective loading; collection-per-tenant is limited to hundreds of loaded collections, and field-based filtering relies entirely on application-layer enforcement.

questions.q: The key sizing principle for Milvus Query Nodes is that the working dataset must fit in aggregate Query Node memory. Which metric dropping below 85% indicates memory pressure and cold-load-dominated p99?
options: milvus_proxy_search_latency_p99
milvus_querynode_cache_hit_rate
milvus_datanode_consume_msg_count
milvus_indexnode_index_task_count
questions.explain: The chapter says to monitor milvus_querynode_cache_hit_rate: anything below 85% indicates memory pressure and means cold segment loading from object storage will dominate p99 latency.
